metadata.title: Remanence Conformance Vectors
metadata.description:
These are the test vectors for the REM-OBJECT, REM-ENCRYPT and REM-PARITY specifications. They let an independent implementation check itself against byte-exact expected results, and let a reader confirm a specification's statements.

The record holds two archives. remanence-test-vectors.tar is the generation-1 archive, the pinned baseline that the published specification text cites by hash. It is deposited here unchanged. remanence-draft-test-vectors.tar holds the review vectors for the current drafts: REM-OBJECT and REM-ENCRYPT vectors, generation-2 REM-PARITY tape images, damage, resume and negative cases, independent verifiers, and a second implementation with its decision files.

The draft archive is for review only. It is not a conformance set, and the frozen set, published when the specifications freeze on 31 July 2027, replaces it. Generation-2 tapes are not readable by generation-1 tooling.

metadata.title: The Remanence Formats, Explained
metadata.description:
This is a plain-language companion to the REM-OBJECT Core Format, REM-ENCRYPT and REM-PARITY specifications. It sets out the problem of keeping a large archive readable for decades, and explains why the formats are shaped as they are. It is informative only. Where it and a specification disagree, the specification governs.

The companion does not freeze. It is revised whenever a passage can be made clearer or a specification changes. Revision 1.2 follows the review draft of REM-PARITY that describes generation 2 of the tape layout. The specifications it explains are review drafts, to be frozen on 31 July 2027.

Generation-2 tapes are not readable by generation-1 tooling, and the companion says so in its maturity note.

It is written for readers in digital preservation who want the reasoning before the byte tables.

metadata.title: REM-OBJECT Core Format 1.0: Specification
metadata.description:
This is the specification of the REM-OBJECT Core Format: a backend-independent byte format for large archival objects. An object bundles named file payloads into one self-describing unit, a constrained POSIX pax tar stream with a SHA-256 identity for each file, addressing of byte ranges by calculation, and a deterministic CBOR manifest.

This is a review draft and not the frozen revision. Comments close on 30 April 2027, and the specifications are to be frozen on 31 July 2027.

The generation distinction concerns the tape layout of REM-PARITY. It does not change this format: revision 1.0.0-draft.4 changes no byte of a valid object relative to 1.0.0-draft.3.

The document is intended to let a digital preservation reader read an archived object with ordinary tools and verify its contents. No standards body has reviewed it.

metadata.title: REM-ENCRYPT 1.0: Specification
metadata.description:
This is the specification of REM-ENCRYPT, an authenticated, confidential envelope around the canonical plaintext object of the REM-OBJECT Core Format. It hides the object's member names, sizes, count, manifest and payload. A plaintext and an encrypted copy of an object share one logical identity.

This is a review draft and not the frozen revision. Comments close on 30 April 2027, and the specifications are to be frozen on 31 July 2027.

The generation distinction concerns the tape layout of REM-PARITY. It does not change this format: revision 1.0.0-draft.4 changes no byte of a valid envelope relative to 1.0.0-draft.3.

Key wrapping uses HPKE with the X-Wing hybrid KEM (ML-KEM-768 with X25519). No standards body has reviewed the document.

metadata.title: Rem Tape Parity (REM-PARITY) Format 1.0: Specification
metadata.description:
This is the specification of the REM-PARITY tape layout: how an archive is laid out on LTO tape with sidecar erasure-coded parity, a bootstrap block and a terminal index, so that a tape can be scanned, checked and repaired without any catalog. It defines what a writer, scanner, recoverer, resumer and verifier do.

This is a review draft and not the frozen revision. Comments close on 30 April 2027, and the specifications are to be frozen on 31 July 2027.

Generation-2 tapes, which current Remanence software writes, are not readable by generation-1 tooling, and generation-1 tapes are not readable by generation-2 readers. This revision governs generation 2 only.

The document is intended to let a digital preservation reader recover data from a damaged tape from the text alone. No standards body has reviewed it.
